reuse.why: Most consumers share getWorstCaseAmount and reuse getApproxNumberThreshold, but API serialization and previews retain independent amount decisions.

duplication.why: The API helper repeats missing/number/range dispatch, and previews retain another dispatch instead of delegating the complete decision.

placement.why: The shared schedules module is appropriate for the policy, but getExpectedAmount places a competing policy inside API serialization.

scope.why: The changes stay focused on schedule amount planning, API exposure, associated types, tests, and release notes.

maintainability.why: Maintainers must coordinate multiple amount-policy implementations, while optional operator arguments allow consumers to omit information the shared decision needs.

bypasses_abstraction.where: api-models.ts:getExpectedAmount bypasses the shared schedule amount helper; schedules.ts:computeSchedulePreviewTransactions delegates only range selection and retains its own dispatch.

disguised_duplication.where: api-models.ts:getExpectedAmount reshapes the existing amount dispatch under a new name, while computeSchedulePreviewTransactions extracts range arithmetic but preserves the surrounding duplicated decision.

abstraction_drift.where: Operator parameters appear on getWorstCaseAmount and getScheduledAmount, with one isapprox branch; API serialization and preview generation continue to decide amounts outside the complete shared policy.
